mainEntity.name: Can impacted wisdom teeth cause dental implants to fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Impacted wisdom teeth do not directly cause implant failure, but the complications they produce — such as localised bone loss, infection, or gum disease — can create an environment where implant success is compromised. If an impacted wisdom tooth has damaged the bone in the area where an implant is planned, additional procedures such as bone grafting may be required before implant placement can proceed safely. Your dentist will assess the specific situation and advise accordingly.

mainEntity.name: How long after wisdom tooth removal can I get a dental implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single answer to this question, as healing times vary between individuals and depend on the complexity of the extraction, the amount of bone involved, and whether any bone loss or infection was present. In straightforward cases, a dentist may recommend waiting approximately three to six months for adequate healing before implant placement. In cases involving bone grafting or significant tissue repair, longer periods may be required. Your dentist will provide a personalised timeline following assessment.

mainEntity.name: Will my dentist always know if I have impacted wisdom teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Impacted wisdom teeth are not always visible during a routine oral examination, particularly if they are fully submerged beneath the gumline. Dental X-rays are essential for identifying impacted teeth and assessing their position, angle, and proximity to adjacent structures. This is one reason why regular dental check-ups that include periodic radiographic assessment are important, especially during the years when wisdom teeth typically develop.

mainEntity.name: Can misaligned wisdom teeth damage the teeth next to them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, misaligned wisdom teeth — particularly those growing at an angle towards adjacent molars — can place pressure on neighbouring teeth, potentially contributing to root resorption (where the root of the adjacent tooth gradually breaks down), decay in hard-to-clean areas, and structural damage. The extent of any damage depends on the angle of the wisdom tooth, the duration of the problem, and how promptly it is identified and managed.

mainEntity.name: Is it possible to have dental implants placed at the same time as wisdom tooth extraction?

acceptedAnswer.text: In certain carefully selected cases, it may be possible to extract a wisdom tooth and place a dental implant in the same surgical session. However, this approach depends on several clinical factors, including the condition of the bone, the absence of active infection, and the proximity of the two sites. It is not appropriate in all circumstances and requires careful pre-operative planning. Your dental team will advise on whether same-session treatment is suitable in your case.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I choose not to treat impacted wisdom teeth before getting implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing to proceed with implant treatment without addressing problematic impacted wisdom teeth carries a potential risk of ongoing or worsening complications at the implant site. If the impacted tooth is associated with infection or bone loss, these issues could affect the long-term stability of the implant. That said, not all impacted wisdom teeth require treatment. A dentist will assess the risk on a case-by-case basis and will explain the reasoning behind any recommendation clearly.
